ACME UNIVERSITY ACADEMIC AND EMPLOYMENT POLICY
Version 3.1 -- Effective 1 January 2024

Chapter-1
Preliminary

1. Short title and commencement: This policy shall be called the Acme
University Academic and Employment Policy, 2024. It shall come into force on
the first day of January 2024.

2. Definitions: Unless the context otherwise requires, in this policy,
a. "Institution" means Acme University and includes all of its constituent
   campuses and research centres.
b. "Staff member" means any person appointed to a salaried position at the
   Institution, and includes probationary and fixed-term appointees.
c. "Student" means any person enrolled in a degree or diploma programme of the
   Institution.
d. "Working day" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public
   holiday declared by the Institution.

Chapter-2
Appointment and Probation

3. Probation period: Every staff member appointed to a permanent position
shall serve a probation period of three months from the date of joining. The
probation period shall not exceed three months, and shall not be extended.
Provided that where a staff member has been absent for more than fifteen
consecutive working days during probation, the Institution may extend the
probation by the length of that absence.

4. Confirmation of appointment: A staff member who completes the probation
period satisfactorily shall be deemed confirmed in the position. The
Institution shall issue a written confirmation within fifteen working days of
the completion of probation.

5. Termination during probation: The Institution may terminate the appointment
of a probationary staff member by giving seven days written notice, without
assigning any reason.

Chapter-3
Leave

6. Annual leave: Every confirmed staff member shall be entitled to eighteen
days of paid annual leave in each calendar year. Unused annual leave may be
accumulated up to a maximum of forty-five days.

7. Sick leave: Every staff member shall be entitled to twelve days of paid
sick leave in each calendar year. Sick leave exceeding three consecutive days
shall be supported by a certificate from a registered medical practitioner.

8. Maternity leave: A female staff member shall be entitled to ninety-eight
days of paid maternity leave. Such leave may commence up to fifteen days
before the expected date of delivery.

9. Bereavement leave: A staff member shall be entitled to thirteen days of
paid bereavement leave on the death of an immediate family member.

Chapter-4
Working Hours and Remuneration

10. Working hours: No staff member shall be required to work for more than
eight hours in a day or forty-eight hours in a week. A rest interval of not
less than thirty minutes shall be provided after five continuous hours of work.

11. Overtime: Where a staff member works beyond the hours specified in section
10, the Institution shall pay overtime at one and one-half times the ordinary
rate of remuneration. No staff member shall be required to work more than
twenty hours of overtime in a week.

12. Payment of remuneration: Remuneration shall be paid within seven days of
the end of each calendar month, by direct transfer to the staff member's bank
account.

Chapter-5
Academic Integrity

13. Plagiarism: A student who submits work that is not their own shall be
subject to disciplinary proceedings. A first offence shall attract a written
warning and a mark of zero for the assessment concerned.

14. Repeated offences: A second offence of plagiarism shall attract suspension
for one academic semester. A third offence shall attract expulsion from the
Institution.

15. Appeals: A student may appeal a disciplinary decision to the Academic
Appeals Committee within twenty-one days of being notified of the decision.
The Committee shall decide the appeal within thirty working days.

Chapter-6
Grievances

16. Grievance procedure: A staff member or student with a grievance shall
submit it in writing to the Grievance Officer. The Grievance Officer shall
acknowledge receipt within three working days and shall resolve the grievance
within twenty-one working days.

17. Confidentiality: All grievance proceedings shall be kept confidential, and
no record of a grievance shall be placed in a staff member's personnel file
unless a disciplinary sanction results from it.
